input_schema.description: Optional Lab hardware.compute contract; sizes are allocations, not CPU models.
input_schema.title: LabCompute

schema.device: Required: cpu (CPU-only), gpu (GPU required), or either (both supported).
schema.cpu_cores: Optional positive minimum CPU allocation, finite number.
schema.memory_mb: Optional positive integer minimum host RAM in MiB.
schema.gpu_count: Optional positive integer minimum GPU count for GPU profiles.
schema.gpu_type: Optional exact GPU catalog type; compare case-insensitively.
schema.recommended_profile: Optional catalog name, advisory and separate from requirements.

rules: Read compute_profile_list before creating/updating a Lab or preparing compute; never invent profile IDs or hardcode the available catalog.
Declare actual execution support based on the code and dependencies. A CUDA-only component requires device=gpu; either requires a working CPU and GPU path.
Aggregate runnable component requirements into Lab-level hardware.compute; reassess requirements whenever components, dependencies or workload change.
CPU cores and memory are minimum allocations, not a CPU vendor or model. memory_mb is host RAM; GPU VRAM minimums are not currently exposed or enforceable and must not be claimed.
Use manifest_patch to update hardware.compute in an approval-bound immutable Lab revision. Unknown compute fields and contradictory CPU/GPU declarations block validation.
Pass a discovered item id as compute_profile_id in run_prepare or each experiment arm. Explicit selection overrides recommendations but cannot bypass requirements or provider availability.
Omitting compute_profile_id uses a compatible recommendation, then the configured compatible default/catalog order. Legacy Labs retain their established default selection.
Review resolved provider, profile, CPU, RAM, GPU, timeout and provider-cost estimate before approval. The provider is platform-controlled; no Modal credentials or local repository are needed.
Profile discovery checks configuration/account access, not live capacity. run_prepare is the authoritative compatibility and cost preflight; never silently replace an unavailable explicit profile.
Hardware requirements are enforced for managed runs; local host checks remain separate evidence and do not certify managed availability.

visualization.guidance: Almost every new Lab and scientific result model needs a useful visualization of actual computed outputs. Available renderers: timeseries (time evolution), bar (categories), scatter (observed versus predicted), heatmap (matrices/spatial fields), graph (networks), table (exact values), image (scientific images/overlays), structure3d (coordinates), and text (interpretation/caveats). Choose by the user's question; a table is not the default for every result. Before authoring, read get_biosimulant_authoring_contract topic visualization. Record visuals in MRS/MTS, implement BioModule.visualize() from computed state and declare lab.yaml visualization requirements. Infrastructure-only components may opt out with a recorded reason. Ad-hoc chat charts do not satisfy reusable Lab visualization requirements. Retain typed scientific outputs alongside visuals.

timeseries.use_when: Changes over time; include time and quantity units

bar.use_when: Compare categories, endpoint counts or scenario summaries

scatter.use_when: Compare measurements, predictions, residuals or uncertainty

heatmap.use_when: Matrices, spatial fields, correlations or parameter sweeps

graph.use_when: Measured or modeled networks and dependencies

table.use_when: Exact values and metadata; accompany a plot when one aids interpretation

image.use_when: Scientific images, annotations, segmentation masks and overlays

data.alt: Detected colonies with numbered bounding boxes
data.caption: Computed detections; inspect low-confidence regions.

structure3d.use_when: Molecular or structural coordinates (PDB/mmCIF common subset)

text.use_when: Interpretation, caveats, abstentions or a result with no numeric plot

data.text: Interpret the computed result within its declared intended use.

catalog.custom_renderers: Unsupported unless a renderer is registered in every target client; v1 uses the nine portable kinds.

visualization.placement: Declare visualization at the top level of lab.yaml; module names are actual composed runtime aliases (including child prefixes).
visualization.lifecycle: visualize() reads computed state after execute; use ONCE_AFTER_RUN for finite downstream analysis with real typed wiring. Do not perform inference, evolve scientific state or fabricate results in visualize().
visualization.assets: Use data.source={kind: artifact, path: outputs/annotated.png} for images or structure files and emit the same path on a typed file output. Managed execution retains and rewrites it to artifact_id. Reopened clients fetch through authorized run context; never persist temporary paths or expiring URLs as the delivered visual. Small images may use a complete data:image/...;base64,... URI, not raw base64.
visualization.acceptance: Test the composed CLI results, payload validity, labels/units, plotted values against typed outputs, retained assets, and reopening. Required visual failure blocks qualification/publication while scientific outputs remain available. Runtime visualization diagnostics expose failures; visual count alone is insufficient.
visualization.specifications: MRS: user question, expected view, source outputs, units, intended-use caveats, usability acceptance and justified opt-outs. MTS: chosen render/schema_version, owning module, typed wiring, lifecycle, preview limits, artifact retention and executable checks. Almost every Lab needs a view; infrastructure-only components may opt out with a nonempty reason.
visualization.studio_charts: create_visualization creates a separate chat resource; it does not implement reusable model/lab visualize().

required_api: inputs() -> mapping[str, SignalSpec] when inputs exist
outputs() -> mapping[str, SignalSpec] when outputs exist
execute(inputs, *, context) for all newly authored modules
an explicit ExecutionPolicy for every newly authored module
advance_window(start, end) plus set_inputs()/get_outputs() remains supported for imported temporal modules that require settle participation
snapshot() and restore(snapshot) for stateful modules
biomodule.units: Declare output units with SignalSpec.emitted_unit and accepted input units with AcceptedSignalProfile entries in SignalSpec.accepted_profiles. The runtime does not silently convert units; use an explicit converter BioModule when needed.
biomodule.input_values: Connected values in execute(inputs, *, context) are BioSignal objects. Read the scientific payload from inputs['port'].value before passing it to domain logic; do not treat the signal wrapper as a bare dict, list, or number.
biomodule.validation: Reject biologically invalid inputs at the component boundary and test the exact port names, signal kinds, dtypes, shapes, units, and state lifecycle. A direct BioModule used in Lab wiring must implement typed inputs() and outputs() methods; model.yaml io is descriptive metadata and does not replace the runtime methods.
biomodule.runtime_observability: The terminal result or summary BioModule must implement visualize() so the actual composed-run observables are serialized under visuals in the CLI results JSON. Domain acceptance must inspect that runtime JSON; directly calling components in a test is useful unit coverage but is not evidence that the composed Lab propagated signals correctly.
biomodule.window_performance: New temporal modules implement execute(inputs, *, context), explicitly use ExecutionPolicy.EACH_WINDOW, and read context.window_start/window_end. Import ExecutionPolicy from biosim (or biosimulant). Finite preprocessing and inference use ExecutionPolicy.ONCE_BEFORE_RUN; final analysis and export use ExecutionPolicy.ONCE_AFTER_RUN. An AI component that participates in temporal feedback uses ExecutionPolicy.EACH_WINDOW. Never quote an uppercase enum member name: the only accepted string values are once_before_run, each_window, and once_after_run. Existing advance_window() modules remain supported for compatibility and zero-time settle participation. Never override both hooks, generate the unreleased one-argument execute signature, invent wrapper-local run-once caches, or perform a full-horizon integration once per communication window. Ask for intended temporal semantics when the correct policy is ambiguous.
biomodule.manifest_execution_policy: Repeat the class's policy in model.yaml as biosim.execution_policy using the exact lowercase value (once_before_run, each_window, or once_after_run), next to biosim.entrypoint. It must match the Python execution_policy attribute: the runtime refuses to load a model whose declaration disagrees, and Studio and the Hub use it to decide whether duration and communication_step apply without importing model code. Leave biosim.execution_policy out when the policy depends on parameters or other runtime values, for example when __init__ selects it from a mode argument.

managed_runtime.rule: The system /usr/bin/python does not contain biosim. Do not probe for it. Biosimulant CLI commands use the managed runtime automatically.
managed_runtime.dependency_environment: After ensure_python_environment succeeds, its primary environment contains the exact managed Biosimulant/Biosim release plus all resolved scientific dependencies. Use its python and biosimulant executables for every direct Python command, Lab command, and acceptance test that imports those dependencies; do not mix that code with /opt/biosimulant/cli/bin/python.

record_signal_template.emission: return {'record': dict(payload)}  # BioWorld validates, binds, and timestamps it
record_signal_template.rule: SignalSpec.record schema values are dtypes. Use a record-level emitted or accepted unit only when every numeric field shares that unit; otherwise split ports or make field units explicit in the typed schema and tests.

event_signal_contract.emission: EventSignal(source='doser', name='dose_event', value={'event_id': event_id, 'dose_mg': dose_mg}, emitted_at=event_time, spec=self.outputs()['dose_event'])
event_signal_contract.runtime_semantics: BioWorld delivers an event at most once per connection for a strictly increasing emitted_at timestamp and preserves that delivery cursor across snapshot/restore. Emit an event only when it becomes due. Re-returning the same timestamp is suppressed, and a later delivery with an equal or older timestamp is also suppressed. Multiple distinct events at the same time on one port must therefore be represented as one schema-bound batch event or as distinct event ports.
event_signal_contract.rule: Represent discrete interventions with SignalSpec.event and EventSignal, not a state RecordSignal that is replayed every communication window. Include a stable event_id when domain-level deduplication or auditability matters; the runtime cursor is timestamp-based, not an event-ID registry. Test missing, duplicate, same-time, stale, and out-of-order events through the composed runtime, including after snapshot/restore.
